axis: adaptive robust-intensity DoG threshold (median + k*1.4826*MAD per volume) replacing the fixed percentile-92 cutoff, to stop dataset-scale over-detection

axis: division-aware linking (link.allow_division on) with over-split control (division_distance in {7,5,3,2}, division_max_sibling_ratio in {0,3,2,1.5}) as a score lever on top of the detect-link-dog-v4-shorttrack champion; single-variable ablation (deterministic pipeline => same-seed A/B)
hypothesis: The official metric is adjusted_edge_jaccard + 0.1*division_jaccard, and the champion runs allow_division=False so its division Jaccard is 0.0 (6bba_05db0fb1 has 3 GT divisions, all missed). Zebrafish embryogenesis is division-heavy, so division-aware linking (attach a leftover t+1 detection as a matched parent's balanced second daughter) should recover division TP and raise the composite score without regressing edge Jaccard, given over-split suppression (tighter division_distance + sibling-balance ratio gate).
evidence: Screened allow_division=True over a 4x4 grid (division_distance {7,5,3,2} x division_max_sibling_ratio {0,3,2,1.5}) on the SOT-2761 leak-free CV, detection frozen (DoG-v3 mad_k=3.0) and computed once per family. Baseline champion (allow_division=False): micro_adj 0.6649, division_jaccard 0.0, score 0.6649. Every division variant REGRESSES: best composite is dd=5.0/ratio=1.5 = score 0.6646 (delta -0.0003) with division_jaccard 0.0625 but per-dataset edge adj regresses on 3/4 families (6bba_05b6850b 0.5700->0.5616, 6bba_05db0fb1 0.7310->0.7261, 44b6_0113de3b 0.8895->0.8887) so no_per_dataset_regression=False. The economics do not close: at dd=5/ratio=1.5 division recovers only 1 of 3 GT divisions (6bba_05db0fb1 tp=1/fp=3/fn=2) while spraying 10 FP forks on the dense 6bba_05b6850b family; the 0.1 division weight (+0.0063 max here) cannot pay for the edge-Jaccard cost of the added fork edges on the dense families. Tightening division_distance to 2um makes division essentially never fire (div_j 0.0, score == champion 0.6649) - no free divisions available at close range. Over-split knobs behave exactly as designed (tighter dd + balance ratio raise div_j per fork and cut edge damage) but never net positive AND never pass the no-regression gate. Independently re-scored through the real champion_params(config)->run_pipeline + evaluate_cv (guards the new division_max_sibling_ratio plumbing, mirrors the SOT-2369 confirm): baseline 0.6649, challenger dd5/ratio1.5 0.6646 (delta -0.0003, no_reg=False) - reproduces the screen. Champion MAINTAINED at detect-link-dog-v4-shorttrack (allow_division=False); champion/config.json + registry.json + EMBEDDED_CHAMPION_CONFIG unchanged. The division over-split mechanism (link.division_max_sibling_ratio, default 0.0 = off) is kept as a documented default-off knob exactly as the SOT-2369 motion lever (velocity_gain) was kept after its rejection. No Kaggle submission. See experiments/sot2762/{screen_division,confirm_division}.json and docs/ai/sot-2762-division-linking.md.

axis: gap-closing 2nd-step LAP linking (Jaqaman/TrackMate: bridge fragment tail@t -> head@t+g for 2<=g<=max_frame_gap within gap_distance um, run before short-track prune) on top of the detect-link-dog-v4-shorttrack champion; single-variable ablation (deterministic pipeline => same-seed A/B), grid max_frame_gap {2,3} x gap_distance {7,10,14}um
hypothesis: The champion links only consecutive frames, so a cell missed in one detection frame ends its track (the standard FN-edge source). Classical gap-closing (public 'Learned Graph w/ Gap Recovery', Jaqaman 2nd step / TrackMate) bridges fragments across missing detections; a CPU numpy/scipy LAP second step should recover FN edges and raise the score, given the gap-close-then-reprune interaction with short-track pruning.
evidence: DECISIVE METRIC CONSTRAINT: the edge metric (edge_metric._sanitise_pred_edges step 1) keeps only consecutive-frame edges (t_target-t_source==1), so a bridge edge spanning a gap is dropped before scoring (never TP, never FP). Gap-closing therefore has no direct edge lever; its only effect is changing which nodes survive the min_track_length=4 prune (gap-close runs before prune), which feeds the per-timepoint <=7um node matching. On the SOT-2761 leak-free CV (DoG-v3 mad_k=3.0 frozen, detection computed once per family, re-linked per variant), EVERY variant regresses and none passes no-regression; monotone with looseness: best (least-bad) mfg=2/gd=7 micro-adj 0.6649->0.6509 (delta -0.0140, ΔTP -12/ΔFP +23/ΔFN +12), worst mfg=3/gd=14 0.6323 (-0.0326, ΔTP -34). Per-dataset matched-edge accounting at mfg2/gd7 vs champion floor: 44b6_0113de3b adj 0.8895->0.8875 ΔTP0/ΔFP0/ΔFN0 +560 nodes (PURE node-count penalty: bridges only stitched noise fragments carrying no evaluable edge); 44b6_0b24845f 0.6817->0.6764 ΔTP0/ΔFP0/ΔFN0 +2538 nodes (same); 6bba_05b6850b 0.5700->0.5433 ΔTP -13/ΔFP +18/ΔFN +13 +643 nodes (MATCHING CORRUPTION: resurrected nodes steal per-timepoint matches, real edges->FN, spurious->FP); 6bba_05db0fb1 0.7310->0.7275 ΔTP +1/ΔFP +5/ΔFN -1 +1522 nodes (+1 TP swamped by node penalty). FN-recovery hypothesis REFUTED: net ΔFN is +12 (positive) => gap-closing recovered NO real FN edges anywhere. The short-track prune already correctly removes these short fragments as noise (SOT-2369 thesis); gap-closing works against it by resurrecting noise. The only alternative order (gap-close AFTER prune, stitching already-surviving long tracks) is a strict no-op on this metric (no node change, bridge edge dropped), so no admissible ordering nets positive. Independently reproduced through the real champion_params(config)->run_pipeline + evaluate_cv (guards the new max_frame_gap/gap_distance plumbing, champion default stays max_frame_gap=1 off): baseline 0.6649, challenger mfg2/gd7 0.6509 (delta -0.0140, no_reg=False). Champion MAINTAINED at detect-link-dog-v4-shorttrack; champion/config.json + registry.json + EMBEDDED_CHAMPION_CONFIG unchanged. gap-closing kept as a documented default-off knob (link.max_frame_gap=1 default, link.gap_distance) as SOT-2369 velocity_gain and SOT-2762 division_max_sibling_ratio were kept after rejection. 71 pytest + exec-compat gate green. No Kaggle submission. See experiments/sot2763/{screen_gap_closing,confirm_gap_closing}.json and docs/ai/sot-2763-gap-closing.md.

Decompose into detection-stage ports of classical CPU-portable methods from the competition's own top-solution/baseline lineage + light-sheet nucleus-detection literature.
hypothesis: The champion detector is a SINGLE-scale DoG (foreground sigma [1,2,2] vox, background [2,6,6]) + adaptive-MAD threshold + NMS local-maxima. It is tuned to one blob radius and cannot split touching nuclei, so on the dense 6bba families matched-edge FN/FP dominate (6bba_05b6850b adj 0.5700 FN194, 6bba_05db0fb1 adj 0.7310 FN210). Three CPU numpy/scipy-portable detection-stage levers from the public frontier/baseline lineage should raise detection recall/precision balance across families without needing GPU weights: (1) multi-scale scale-space DoG/LoG blob detection (per-voxel max response over a small radius bank) to catch cells across sizes; (2) watershed splitting of merged detections seeded by regional/h-maxima to separate spatially-overlapping nuclei on the dense families; (3) per-volume robust quantile intensity normalization before DoG (the official royerlab baseline uses quantile normalization) to stabilize the adaptive threshold under the embryo's strong intensity drift and recover dim cells.
evidence: Web research of the competition's own solution lineage + light-sheet nucleus-detection literature (recorded for the child ports): (a) royerlab official baseline https://github.com/royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition = 3D TemporalUNet3D detection map + local-max suppression + cross-attention transformer linking, with QUANTILE NORMALIZATION of inputs and sparse (GT-only) supervision; GPU deep part is NON-portable (no weights/no-internet/CPU kernel) but the quantile-normalization + local-max-suppression classical steps are portable. (c) light-sheet zebrafish nucleus-detection literature confirms the portable detection levers: scale-space / Hessian-DoG (HDoG) multi-radius blob detection (Scale space detector, ScienceDirect S2589004222011488) and DoG+watershed / h-maxima seeding to separate spatially-overlapping nuclei in 3D nnU-Net pipelines (PMC11580962, ScienceDirect S2589004226017517). axis: per-volume robust quantile intensity normalization ([plow,phigh] clip -> [0,1]) before DoG (DetectParams.intensity_norm)
hypothesis: royerlab's public baseline contrast-stretches each volume before detection; feeding raw intensity lets the adaptive-MAD threshold drift across the embryo brightness change and drop dim family/timepoint cells, so a per-volume percentile clip->[0,1] rescale before the DoG should stabilise the threshold and recover dim-cell recall (lower edge FN).
evidence: SOT-2761 leak-free CV, frozen champion downstream (DoG-v3 mad_k=3.0 + short-track mtl=4), only DetectParams.intensity_norm varied; deterministic same-seed A/B. baseline_none reproduces champion 0.6649 exactly. Every quantile band regresses monotonically with clip aggressiveness and fails the gate (micro improvement AND per-dataset no-regression): q_p1_p99.9=0.6511 (-0.0138), q_p0.5_p99.5=0.6159 (-0.049), q_p1_p99=0.5887 (-0.0762), q_p2_p98=0.5451 (-0.1198), q_p5_p95=0.5138 (-0.1511); none no-regression. Hypothesis refuted: recall got WORSE, not better - under q_p1_p99 the dim/sparse 6bba_05b6850b went edge TP 651->528, FN 194->317, FP 215->307, and the clean 44b6_0113de3b 47/2/3 -> 44/10/6. Root cause: the detector already handles brightness drift via DoG local-contrast + robust per-volume MAD z-score (median+3*1.4826*MAD); a global percentile clip compresses dynamic range and saturates the bright tail where nuclei live, shrinking DoG contrast for dim nuclei (FN up) and admitting noise (FP up). Champion unchanged; knob kept default-off (None reproduces exactly), pytest+exec-compat green. No Kaggle submission. See experiments/sot2776/screen_quantile_norm.json and docs/ai/sot-2776-quantile-norm.md.

axis: watershed nucleus splitting (h-maxima seeding -> marker-controlled nearest-seed partition) on the DoG response to split fused nuclei and recover matched-edge TP on the dense 6bba families; new default-off DetectParams.watershed, detection variable, single-variable A/B on the SOT-2761 leak-free CV
hypothesis: The champion detector reports one centroid per NMS local maximum, so two nuclei whose blurred DoG blobs merge into a single response peak collapse to one detection (the matched-edge FN/FP source on the dense 6bba families: 6bba_05b6850b adj 0.5700 FN194, 6bba_05db0fb1 adj 0.7310 FN210). Classical light-sheet nucleus splitting (h-maxima seeding + marker-controlled watershed, numpy/scipy only) should split the fused blobs and recover dense-family TP without needing GPU weights.
evidence: SOT-2761 leak-free CV, downstream frozen champion (DoG-v3 mad_k=3.0 + short-track mtl=4), only DetectParams.watershed varied; deterministic same-seed A/B. baseline_none reproduces champion 0.6649 exactly.
